findings.message: checkout without persist-credentials: false — tokens may leak
findings.remediation: Use persist-credentials: false when checking out external/untrusted repositories.
findings.impact: Checkout without persist-credentials: false leaves GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config for any process to read.
findings.attack_vector: actions/checkout defaults to persist-credentials: true — token leaks via .git/config.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Grant write scopes only to the job that needs them and keep all other scopes read-only or none.
findings.impact: A compromised workflow step can modify repository content, packages, deployments, checks, or security records.
findings.attack_vector: A permissions block grants write access to a sensitive GITHUB_TOKEN scope.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: dynamically imports code from a variable path (3 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Use static imports with allowlisted modules; avoid dynamic import() with variable arguments.
findings.impact: Dynamic import() with variable paths allows loading arbitrary modules at runtime.
findings.attack_vector: import(variablePath) — attacker controls the path to inject malicious modules.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: contains 1 line(s) longer than 500 characters (possible minified/obfuscated code)
findings.remediation: Review extremely long lines; they may contain hidden logic.
findings.impact: Extremely long lines hide obfuscated or minified code from human review.
findings.attack_vector: Lines > 500 chars — code is structured to evade visual inspection.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: reads environment secrets and makes network requests in the same file
findings.remediation: Separate secret handling from network requests; never combine in the same code flow.
findings.impact: Environment secrets combined with network requests create a direct exfiltration channel.
findings.attack_vector: process.env.* + fetch/http.request in same file — secrets flow to external endpoints.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: disables TLS verification or references plaintext HTTP transport (4 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Use HTTPS and keep TLS certificate verification enabled.
findings.impact: Disabling TLS verification or using plaintext HTTP allows MITM interception of all traffic.
findings.attack_vector: rejectUnauthorized: false or http:// URL — attacker can intercept/modify all requests.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses eval() or new Function() to execute dynamically generated code
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use fixed allowlisted implementations.
findings.impact: Dynamic eval/Function allows execution of arbitrary injected code, bypassing all static defenses.
findings.attack_vector: User input or fetched data flows into eval()/new Function() without sanitization.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
